attributes.name: ypy-signals
attributes.description: Declares signals and makes the element a scope: its signals are visible to the element and its descendants. Values are literals. An existing signal keeps its value when the markup is processed again, so a morph does not reset the state. A name that starts with `_` is local and never sent to the server.
attributes.syntax: `name: literal, other: literal` (braces optional, JSON works too)

attributes.name: ypy-signals.server
attributes.description: Declares server-owned signals. The client cannot write them; only a server patch or the markup of this declaration changes them. This is a convenience of the UI, not security: the server must sign and verify the values it owns.

attributes.name: ypy-signals.local
attributes.description: Declares signals persisted in `localStorage` under the key `ypy-signals:<id>`. The element needs an `id`. Stored values replace the declared defaults, only for keys the markup declares.

attributes.name: ypy-signals.session
attributes.description: Declares signals persisted in `sessionStorage` under the key `ypy-signals:<id>`. The element needs an `id`.

attributes.name: ypy-computed:*
attributes.description: Declares a derived, read-only signal named after the attribute (`ypy-computed:total-price` defines `$totalPrice`). It follows its dependencies and is never sent to the server.

attributes.name: ypy-bind
attributes.description: Keeps a form control and a signal equal. The signal fills the field and the field writes the signal. By default the field writes on `change`.

modifiers.name: .live
modifiers.description: Write the signal on every `input` event.

modifiers.name: .debounce.<time>
modifiers.description: Write after the user pauses for the time (300ms when omitted). A `change` writes at once.

modifiers.name: .throttle.<time>
modifiers.description: Write at most once per interval with the latest value (300ms when omitted).

attributes.name: ypy-bind:*
attributes.description: Same as `ypy-bind`, with the signal named in the attribute name (`ypy-bind:user-name` binds `$userName`). The value is a path inside the signal.

modifiers.name: .live
modifiers.description: Write the signal on every `input` event.

modifiers.name: .debounce.<time>
modifiers.description: Write after the user pauses for the time (300ms when omitted).

modifiers.name: .throttle.<time>
modifiers.description: Write at most once per interval with the latest value (300ms when omitted).

attributes.name: ypy-text
attributes.description: Sets `textContent` from an expression, as text and never as markup. Objects show as JSON. It runs again when a signal it read changes.

attributes.name: ypy-show
attributes.description: Hides the element (`display: none`) while the expression is false.

attributes.name: ypy-class
attributes.description: Toggles several classes from an object expression, such as `{red: $bad, wide: $w > 3}`. A class name that has a dot goes in this object form.

attributes.name: ypy-class:*
attributes.description: Toggles the class named in the attribute name when the expression is truthy, such as `ypy-class:active="$on"`.

attributes.name: ypy-attr
attributes.description: Sets several attributes from an object expression. `false`, `null` and `undefined` remove an attribute and `true` sets it empty. Refused: `on*` attributes, `srcdoc`, `ypy-*` attributes and script URLs.

attributes.name: ypy-attr:*
attributes.description: Sets the attribute named in the attribute name from the expression. `false`, `null` and `undefined` remove it and `true` sets it empty.

attributes.name: ypy-on:*
attributes.description: Runs signal statements when the DOM event fires, such as `ypy-on:click="$count++; $open = !$open"`. Inside a scope this extension takes the attribute from the core's `ypy-on`: the value is the signal language, not JavaScript. The listener runs in the capture phase on the element, before a request the same element starts.

modifiers.name: .window
modifiers.description: Listen on `window` instead of the element.

modifiers.name: .debounce.<time>
modifiers.description: Run after a pause in the events (300ms when omitted).

modifiers.name: .throttle.<time>
modifiers.description: Run at most once per interval, on the leading edge (300ms when omitted).

attributes.name: ypy-signals-send
attributes.description: Asks for the signals in scope to go with the requests of this element. Signals are sent only when asked: with this attribute on the element, with `ypy-signals-send:inherited` on a container (the nearest value wins), or for the whole page with the config `signals.send`. `false` turns it off again for the element or the container. Signals are never sent to another origin.

values.name: true
values.description: The requests of this element (and of its descendants, when written `:inherited`) carry the signals. An empty value means the same.

values.name: false
values.description: The requests of this element and its descendants do not carry the signals, even when the config asks for them.

events.name: ypy:signals:patch
events.description: Fires before a merge patch is applied to the signals, whether it came from a JSON response or from `ypy.signals.patch()`. Cancel it to discard the patch.

events.name: ypy:signals:readonly
events.description: Fires when a write to a read-only signal (server-owned or computed) was refused. `detail.warn` carries the message and is logged as a warning.

events.name: ypy:signals:error
events.description: Fires when an expression did not parse, a handler or effect threw, or a patch was not usable. The attribute that failed does nothing and the rest of the page keeps working.

config.name: signals.send
config.description: Send the signals in scope with every same-origin request, with no attribute. `ypy-signals-send="false"` turns it off for an element or a container (`:inherited`).

config.name: classes.dirty
config.description: Class added to a signals scope element while it holds unsaved changes. Set it to a space separated list to replace the default.

classes.name: ypy-dirty
classes.description: Applied to a signals scope while a client-owned signal differs from its last saved value. The scope also gets `dirty` in `data-ypy-state` and its `$_dirty` signal is `true`.
